package_info.why_malicious: Version 0.0.7 of the 'strong_password' gem is malicious because it contains obfuscated Ruby code that, when loaded in a Rails application, spawns a persistent background thread which periodically fetches and executes arbitrary Ruby code from a remote Pastebin URL. This enables remote code execution and backdoor installation. The remote payload further hooks into Rack middleware to allow code execution via specially crafted HTTP cookies and exfiltrates sensitive environment data to an external server. The code was published via unauthorized access, making the entire package a severe supply chain threat.

execution_context.trigger: import-time/runtime (when gem is loaded in Rails production environment)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Defines an obfuscated helper method and, if the Rails environment starts with 'p' (i.e., production), spawns a background thread that repeatedly sleeps for a random interval and then fetches and evaluates Ruby code from a remote Pastebin URL. This enables persistent remote code execution in the application context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and creates a persistent background thread that periodically downloads and executes code from an external source at runtime. This is a classic remote code execution backdoor technique, allowing attackers to run arbitrary code on the victim's server without further interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A password strength checking library should never execute remote code, spawn background threads, or make unsolicited network requests. Such behavior is entirely outside the scope of legitimate functionality and introduces severe security risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code loading is sometimes used in plugin systems, but never from untrusted remote sources and never in a security-sensitive library like a password checker.
key_indicators: Obfuscated/minified Ruby code using unconventional method names (e.g., _!)
Use of eval on the result of Net::HTTP.get from a remote URL
Conditional execution based on Rails environment (production only)
Background thread for persistent malicious activity
Direct reference to external Pastebin URL in gem source

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when remote code is fetched and executed by snippet_1)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The payload, when executed, hooks into the Rack::Sendfile middleware by prepending a module that overrides the :call method. It inspects incoming HTTP requests for a cookie named '___id', base64-decodes its value, and evaluates it as Ruby code, enabling arbitrary code execution via web requests. Additionally, it exfiltrates the value of the ENV['URL_HOST'] environment variable to an external server (https://smiley.zzz.com.ua) using an HTTP GET request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting HTTP cookies and evaluating their contents as code is a direct and highly dangerous backdoor, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code remotely via crafted web requests. The exfiltration of environment variables to an external domain constitutes data theft and potential leakage of sensitive configuration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Middleware should never execute code from user-supplied cookies or send environment data to untrusted domains. Such behavior is never legitimate in any context, especially in a security library.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for evaluating base64-decoded data from HTTP cookies in middleware. Dynamic middleware modification is used for instrumentation or logging, but never for code execution from user input.
key_indicators: Dynamic method definition and injection into Rack::Sendfile middleware
Use of eval on base64-decoded data from HTTP_COOKIE
Extraction of code from a cookie named '___id'
Outbound HTTP request to https://smiley.zzz.com.ua with environment data
Obfuscated code structure and use of unconventional method names

attack_chain.action: Malicious gem version 0.0.7 is installed and loaded in a Rails application, triggering execution of obfuscated code.
attack_chain.leads_to: A background thread is started in the production environment, enabling persistent malicious activity.

attack_chain.action: The background thread periodically fetches and executes remote Ruby code from a Pastebin URL, introducing attacker-controlled payloads into the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote payload is executed within the application context, escalating the attack.

attack_chain.action: The remote payload hooks into Rack middleware to evaluate base64-decoded code from specially crafted HTTP cookies and exfiltrates environment data to an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can execute arbitrary code via HTTP requests and receive exfiltrated environment data, maintaining full remote control.

behavioral_signatures: Background threads in Ruby gems that fetch and evaluate remote code at runtime
Conditional execution of code based on Rails environment (e.g., only in production)
Obfuscated or minified Ruby code with unconventional method names
Dynamic method injection into Rack middleware (e.g., Rack::Sendfile)
Evaluation of base64-decoded data from HTTP cookies
Outbound HTTP requests to untrusted domains with environment variables
file_indicators: lib/strong_password/strength_checker.rb containing obfuscated or minified Ruby code
References to external Pastebin or similar URLs in gem source code
Unusual method definitions (e.g., def _!) in gem files
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound HTTP requests from application servers to untrusted domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan gem source code for obfuscated or minified Ruby, especially for eval statements that fetch and execute code from remote URLs. Monitor for background threads or conditional code execution based on Rails environment. Detect dynamic method injection into Rack or other middleware, and look for eval of base64-decoded data from HTTP cookies. Monitor network traffic for requests to known malicious domains (e.g., pastebin.com/raw/xa456PFt, smiley.zzz.com.ua) and for exfiltration of environment variables. Flag any installation or use of 'strong_password' gem version 0.0.7 as malicious and initiate incident response.
